summary: Backend testing for site-specific role content approval bug fix. All 11 tests passed - the fix for Deborah Baeten's issue (user with site-specific admin role unable to approve content) is working correctly.
bug_description: Users with site-specific 'admin' role (in main_site_users collection) but lower global role (in users collection) could not approve content because the approval endpoint only checked global role.
fix_verified: The get_effective_role() function in main_site_context.py correctly checks both global and site-specific roles, returning the higher-privilege role when X-Main-Site-ID header is present.

test_eddy_login_and_global_role.description: Eddy Thijs (eddy.thijs@grk.fm) global role confirmed as 'presenter'

test_pending_approval_without_site_heade.description: GET /api/content/admin/pending-approval WITHOUT X-Main-Site-ID returns 403 (presenter cannot approve)

test_pending_approval_with_site_header_r.description: GET /api/content/admin/pending-approval WITH X-Main-Site-ID: fc37cb22-b93e-4fc8-9d77-818b3af45d35 returns 200 (site admin can approve)

test_approval_with_site_header_returns_2.description: PUT /api/content/{id}/approval WITH X-Main-Site-ID returns 200 and approval_status updated to 'approved'

test_network_admin_can_approve_any_site.description: Network admin (admkoodh@koodh.com) can approve content from any site

test_network_admin_approve_without_heade.description: Network admin can access pending-approval without X-Main-Site-ID header

test_rejection_with_site_header.description: Site admin can reject content when X-Main-Site-ID header is present

test_effective_role_returns_higher_privi.description: get_effective_role() returns site role (admin) over global role (presenter) when header present

test_invalid_site_id_header.description: Invalid site ID in header falls back to global role (403 for presenter)

test_user_without_site_access.description: User without site access uses global role correctly

seed_data_creation: Test content items created and cleaned up during tests
context_for_next_testing_agent: Site-specific role approval is working correctly. The fix uses get_effective_role() in content.py to check both global and site-specific roles. When X-Main-Site-ID header is provided, it looks up the user's site role in main_site_users collection and returns the higher-privilege role.
rca_of_the_issue: The root cause was that content approval endpoints (PUT /api/content/{id}/approval and GET /api/content/admin/pending-approval) only checked the global role from the users collection via require_can_approve_content dependency. Users like Deborah Baeten who had 'presenter' globally but 'admin' on a specific site were denied access. The fix adds get_effective_role() helper that checks both global role and site-specific role (from main_site_users collection) and returns the higher-privilege role.
